statement: For every n satisfying the precondition, whenever sum_zero n returns a result r, the following all hold: (1) len(r) = n; (2) for every i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(r), r[i] != r[j]; (3) interpreting each element of r as an integer, the mathematical sum of r[0], r[1], ..., r[len(r)-1] equals 0.
preconditions: The input n is an I64 with 1 <= n <= 1000.

statement: For every n satisfying the precondition, sum_zero n returns a result r; it does not fail, overflow, panic, or go out of bounds.
preconditions: The input n is an I64 with 1 <= n <= 1000.

statement: For every n satisfying the precondition, whenever sum_zero n returns a result r, there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(r) such that r[i] > 0.
preconditions: The input n is an I64 with 2 <= n <= 1000.

statement: For every n satisfying the precondition, whenever sum_zero n returns a result r, there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(r) such that r[i] < 0.
preconditions: The input n is an I64 with 2 <= n <= 1000.
